signals.name: Lam Research Corp
signals.thesis: Lam Research surged +12.7% to a new 52-week high ($364.80) on massive volume (14.5M vs 3.0M avg) as the entire semiconductor equipment complex ripped higher. KLAC led with +12.9%. AMAT +11.2%. The sector is pricing in sustained AI capex demand and a potential CHIPS Act spending acceleration. LRCX's etch and deposition tools are critical for advanced node manufacturing. RSI 67.7 provides room to run before overextension. EMA20 ($316) well below price = momentum confirmed. Entry on pullback from today's surge to $355 zone gives a clean 2:1 R/R with stop below the breakout level.

signals.name: Caterpillar Inc
signals.thesis: Caterpillar closed at $897.63 (+4.8%) near its 52-week high ($946.83). The construction and mining equipment giant benefits from the US infrastructure spending cycle and global re-industrialization theme. RSI 52.4 is ideal — strong momentum without overextension. ATR 39.2 implies natural price swings, so the $45 stop width (5%) is appropriate at 1.15x ATR. The industrial sector led broader market gains (+5% XLI) as the risk appetite snapback from yesterday's RISK-OFF selloff drove rotation into cyclicals.

signals.name: GE Aerospace
signals.thesis: GE Aerospace surged +4.4% to $332.76 within striking distance of its 52-week high ($348.48). The aerospace and defense sector benefits from both commercial aviation recovery and defense spending tailwinds. Volume was 3.2M, in line with its average — this is steady institutional buying, not a spike-and-fade. RSI 61.9 is healthy. EMA20 ($315.77) serves as the first pullback target. The entry at $328 on a pullback from today's high gives a clean breakout setup with the stop below the EMA20.

signals.name: Johnson & Johnson
signals.thesis: Johnson & Johnson at $238.33 continues its secular uptrend, trading above both EMA20 ($231) and EMA50 ($230.91). RSI 63.2 confirms momentum without overextension. JNJ is a classic defensive play in EARLY RISK-OFF — healthcare staple with 3.2% dividend yield and uncorrelated returns vs cyclicals (correlation -0.04 with LRCX). The $9 stop (3.8%) is 1.9x ATR ($4.63), giving adequate room while respecting the 8% maximum. 52-week high at $251.71 provides the upside target.

signals.name: Merck & Co Inc
signals.thesis: Merck at $120.76 is approaching its 52-week high ($125.14) after a +1.4% session. RSI 58.8 provides ample headroom. The pharma giant's Keytruda franchise and diversified pipeline make it a defensive growth play — ideal for EARLY RISK-OFF environments. EMA20 ($117.70) provides the pullback floor. Volume at 13.1M was above average, suggesting institutional accumulation. Low correlation with cyclicals (0.13 with LRCX, 0.23 with CAT) adds diversification value to the portfolio.

signals.name: Procter & Gamble Co
signals.thesis: Procter & Gamble at $148.34 is above its EMA20 ($144.89) and EMA50 ($145.42), with RSI 57.8 in a healthy momentum zone. PG is the quintessential defensive play — consumer staples revenue is non-cyclical and benefits from pricing power in mild inflationary environments. In EARLY RISK-OFF, PG typically outperforms the broad market. Low correlation with semis (0.04 with LRCX) and industrials (0.16 with CAT) makes it a portfolio stabilizer. The $7 stop (4.7%) is 2.2x ATR ($3.15).

signals.name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria
signals.thesis: BBVA surged +5.1% to $23.15 on strong volume (3.3M vs 1.7M avg). The Spanish bank benefits from rising European interest rates and strong domestic loan demand. RSI 55.8 leaves significant room to run. EMA20 ($22.59) is well below price = fresh breakout. BBVA has moderate correlation with European markets (0.75 with EWJ) but low correlation with US defensives (0.07 with JNJ, 0.25 with PG). European financials are benefiting from the ECB's rate stance and improving credit conditions.

signals.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
signals.thesis: Novo Nordisk at $43.96 (+2.7%) is recovering from its multi-month decline from the $81 high. The GLP-1 franchise leader (Ozempic/Wegovy) is trading near its EMA20 ($43.48) and EMA50 ($43.13) — a clean pullback setup. RSI 52.5 is neutral, providing room in both directions. At 10x trailing P/E (down from 35x at highs), NVO offers value in the European healthcare space. Low correlation with US names (0.11 with JNJ, 0.19 with CAT) adds diversification. This is a mean-reversion play on a secular growth name.

signals.name: iShares MSCI Japan ETF
signals.thesis: EWJ surged +3.2% to $92.18, approaching its 52-week high ($94.28). The Nikkei is at 64,217 — the Japanese equity rally is structural, driven by corporate governance reform (TSE listing requirements), a weak yen boosting exporters, and Japan's semiconductor reindustrialization (TSMC Kumamoto, Rapidus). RSI 52.97 is ideal for a breakout continuation. The $4.50 stop (4.9%) is 2.4x ATR ($1.86). EWJ provides APAC diversification with moderate correlation to global risk (0.73 with LRCX, 0.66 with CAT).

signals.name: SPDR Gold Shares
signals.thesis: Gold surged +2.9% to $4,233/oz as safe-haven demand combined with dollar weakness (DXY -0.25%) to drive the strongest one-day rally in weeks. GLD at $386.32 is bouncing from oversold territory (RSI 34.9) — a classic pullback setup. The metal has corrected from its May highs near $510 and is now trading below its EMA20 ($405.64) and EMA50 ($418.29). In EARLY RISK-OFF, gold historically outperforms as central banks and institutions hedge against potential crisis escalation (crisis probability 23.6%). The $20 stop (5.2%) is 2.0x ATR ($9.88), providing adequate room for gold's natural volatility.
